title: Rome-Floyd fire trucks add kits to help those with special needs - NewsBreak
text:
By mburge ,
5 hours ago Linda Patty, life and fire safety educator for the Rome-Floyd Fire Department, shows a seatbelt strap-on that can provide important medical information to emergency responders during Tuesday’s public safety committee meeting. By Mo Burge The Rome-Floyd Fire Department is making an effort to better assist children and adults with special needs.
The department is providing specialized fire safety education and identification seatbelt strap-ons. It’s also equipping fire trucks with kits that include items intended to bring a little calm in emergency situations, said Linda Patty, life and fire safety educator, at a public safety committee meeting Tuesday.
“It’s something I’ve really been trying to push for our special needs community with safety — because fire really doesn’t care who you are or where you live,” Patty said. “I think this is something that will help the community but also help the responders at the same moment.”
The efforts include helping children and those with special needs better understand fire safety and better equip first responders on the scene to identify those who need special consideration in the midst of an emergency situation.
The kits include fidget toys, Spanish sign language and braille — which can help firefighters communicate and assess — and seatbelt strap-ons that make first responders aware of any important medical issues, Patty said.
Also during the meeting, Deputy Fire Chief Brad Robinson announced that graduation for new firefighter recruits is scheduled for Dec. 11 and Rome Police Chief Denise Downer-McKinney said four new graduates from the police academy will be sworn in Dec. 5.
Additionally, both departments said holiday campaigns are under way to help make Christmas brighter for families in the community.
The fire department is working with Toys for Tots and the Christmas Angel program. Toy donations may be dropped off at any fire station.
The police department is adopting a family through the Exchange Club Family Resource Center.
Both departments are participating in the Salvation Army Kettle Drive.
